reviewType: offline retrieval sufficiency; no candidate answer accuracy judgment
reviewer: Codex assistant; not independent professional legal adjudication
method: Read each supplied question, prior frozen expected reference/check and the actual assembled baseline/candidate target text.
Inspected all source identities and searched potentially equivalent passages where the expected source was missing.
Checked operative thresholds/prohibitions/permissions together with explicit exceptions, scope conditions and requested table row/header/footnotes.
Accepted BC 914.1.1 as a parallel source for exterior shaftway markings even though fixture reference names FC 316.
Did not count generic definitions, incidental numerical matches or a rule from another unestablished discipline as decisive evidence.
limitations: This is the previous campaign regression set, so it is development evidence rather than fresh held-out performance.
47/50 decisive-text availability is not 47/50 correct answers; live drafting, applicability reasoning, citation entailment and conversation behavior still need assessment.
No fresh held-out keys or answers were inspected.
Passage completeness was read from source text, not inferred from canonicalContextComplete metadata alone.
The baseline/candidate packets may contain distracting or conflicting provisions beyond the decisive text. This review does not certify their ranking or prompt sufficiency.
Tables 706.3 and 401.5 were inspected as plain text; no rendered-table or import-correctness certification was performed.
Cases 03 and 17 retain previously identified pane-area and hub-drain wording ambiguities. Cases 29 and 50 omit code-family/district cues from their original named-section prompts.
Review compares supplied local corpus text; it does not establish a fully audited amendment/effective-date state for every source.
Cross-reference installation/design details not needed for each narrow question were distinguished from completeness required for a full compliance determination.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: Does ordinary glazing in a swinging door count as a hazardous location?
cases.reviewNote: Door-glazing hazardous-location sentence and all four explicit exceptions are present.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: is door-adjacent glazing hazardous if its nearest edge is within a 24-inch arc and bottom exposed edge 40 inches above the walking surface, with no exception?
cases.reviewNote: The 24-inch door-edge arc, bottom-edge less-than-60-inch condition, and four explicit exceptions are present.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: a 12 sf window has bottom 12 inches above floor, top 60 inches high and walking surface 24 inches away. No exception applies. Is it hazardous?
cases.reviewNote: All four window-glazing criteria and exceptions are present, including exposed area of an individual pane greater than 9 square feet. The question gives window area, so the answer must qualify whether this is individual-pane area.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: does the hazardous-glazing rule for a shower enclosure apply to every pane of multiple glazing?
cases.reviewNote: Wet-surface hazardous location, bottom-edge height condition, express application to every pane, and stated exception are present.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: bottom-stair landing glazing 40 inches above landing and within the specified 60-inch arc is hazardous absent an exception, correct?
cases.reviewNote: Bottom-stair landing height/arc conditions and guard exception are present. Question excludes the exception; full guard-design references are not necessary to this narrow inquiry.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: what ordinary vertical nonabsorbent base height applies to an office toilet room outside a dwelling unit?
cases.reviewNote: Neither packet supplies the 4-inch vertical nonabsorbent toilet-room base requirement. Fixture counts/location and dwelling-unit accessibility are not equivalent finish rules.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: how high must the nonabsorbent wall surface extend within 2 feet of a WC in an ordinary public toilet room?
cases.reviewNote: Neither packet supplies the 4-foot nonabsorbent surface requirement within 2 feet of a water closet. Nonabsorbent water-closet seat material is not an equivalent wall-finish requirement.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: what minimum net glazed area corresponds to a 200 sf room under the ten-percent rule?
cases.reviewNote: The 10-percent net-glazed-area formula, 12-square-foot required-opening baseline, and Group R-3 exception are present.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: what ordinary minimum plan dimension applies to a habitable room other than a kitchen with no exception?
cases.reviewNote: The 8-foot minimum plan dimension and its explicit four exceptions are present; question excludes exceptions.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: can a finished shower compartment be 28 inches in its least dimension just because its area is 950 squareinches?
cases.reviewNote: Both 900-square-inch area and independent 30-inch minimum finished dimension are present with measurement-height conditions.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: do lavatories for customers in public toilet facilities need tempered water?
cases.reviewNote: Public customer/patron/visitor lavatory scope, tempered-water requirement, approved ASSE 1070 device, and point-of-use-heater exception are present.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: may urinals replace 60 percent of required WCs in a toilet room?
cases.reviewNote: The maximum 50-percent water-closet substitution sentence is present.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: what minimum drain-outlet diameter applies to a floor drain?
cases.reviewNote: The minimum 3-inch floor-drain outlet diameter sentence is present.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: must the central washing room of a multifamily building have floor drains?
cases.reviewNote: Central multifamily washing facilities must drain the entire floor area; minimum 3-inch outlets and lint strainers are present.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: may an ordinary drainage line reduce from 4 inches to 3 inches downstream?
cases.reviewNote: Baseline provides the no-downstream-size-reduction sentence and 4-inch-by-3-inch water-closet connection exception. Candidate provides drainage sizing/venting and general rearrangement requirements but no equivalent prohibition.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: may a sanitary tee provide a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage change?
cases.reviewNote: Table 706.3 column labels, sanitary-tee row X/c, dash, dash, and footnotes survive together with the installation rule. This is plain-text table review, not a visual/table-parser certification.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: how far must a hub drain extend above a water-impervious floor?
cases.reviewNote: The entire short hub-drain provision is present. Its wording attaches extending-not-less-than-1-inch to a hub or a pipe ambiguously; presence does not resolve the professional interpretation identified in the prior key audit.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: may a fixture be double trapped?
cases.reviewNote: Candidate supplies the express no-double-trapping sentence and six exceptions in PC 1002.1. Baseline supplies general fixture counts/location and lacks that prohibition.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: what special lot-line rule applies to an outdoor ventilation-air intake on a lot 18 feet wide?
cases.reviewNote: The less-than-20-foot-lot centerline rule and explicit Group R-3 exception are present. Other intake-location conditions are preserved; occupancy still matters for application.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: can a residential outdoor intake screen have 3/4-inch openings?
cases.reviewNote: Table 401.5 retains the residential intake row with minimum 1/4-inch and maximum 1/2-inch openings, clearly distinguished from nonresidential limits.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: may the required outdoor-air quantity be replaced with recirculated air?
cases.reviewNote: The rule prohibits recirculating required outdoor air while allowing excess supply air subject to four listed restrictions. The outdoor-air engineering exception is also retained.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: can transfer air serve as makeup air for a bathroom exhaust system in principle?
cases.reviewNote: Transfer-air permission, recirculation prohibition caveat, required airflow, and direct/transferred-space outdoor-air conditions are present. This supports a qualified in-principle answer; individual ventilation design still requires the applicable table row.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: which detectors control intermittent enclosed-garage ventilation?
cases.reviewNote: Both carbon-monoxide and nitrogen-dioxide detectors and 25-ppm/500-ppb control thresholds are present.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: how low may automatic garage ventilation reduce the airflow rate?
cases.reviewNote: The 0.05-cfm-per-square-foot reduction floor and 0.75-cfm-per-square-foot capability requirement are present.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: does a dryer installation exhausting 250 cfm require makeup air?
cases.reviewNote: The more-than-200-cfm makeup-air trigger and closet-opening/approved-means alternative are present.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: what dampers generally protect permitted ducts through fire walls?
cases.reviewNote: Both listed fire and smoke dampers are required for permitted fire-wall ducts. Complete smoke-damper exception wording is retained; it must not be reduced to an unqualified standby-power alternative.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: does installing a fire damper by itself authorize penetrating an interior exit stair enclosure?
cases.reviewNote: The fire-barrier damper rule expressly prohibits interior-exit-stair penetration except where BC 1023.5 permits it. Detailed BC permission text is not needed to answer that a damper alone grants no permission.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: does the direct-vent exception allow a gas appliance in a sleeping room?
cases.reviewNote: The main sleeping-room prohibition and non-sleeping-only direct-vent exception are present. The related narrower FGC 303.3.1 direct-vent space-heater provision is also supplied and must be distinguished.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: may an appliance rated 400000 Btu/h rely solely on indoor combustion air?
cases.reviewNote: FGC 304.5 includes the greater-than-350000-Btu/h outdoor-only condition and indoor-air-volume context. The section-number removal leaves appliance/fuel applicability less explicit, so source presence supports a qualified answer rather than a universal appliance conclusion.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: what is the minimum dimension of an outdoor combustion-air opening?
cases.reviewNote: The 3-inch minimum air-opening dimension and outdoor supply/DEP qualification are present.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: are threaded gas-piping elbows among the fittings permitted in concealed locations?
cases.reviewNote: The complete permitted concealed-fitting list contains threaded elbows, tees and couplings and welded fittings.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: how far must a protective sleeve for below-grade gas piping project beyond the inside and outside foundation wall?
cases.reviewNote: The 1-inch inside/4-inch outside sleeve projection, gas-provider qualification, and sealed/waterproof annular-space condition are present.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: what minimum elevation above the roof applies to outdoor gas piping crossing the roof?
cases.reviewNote: Candidate supplies the 3-1/2-inch above-roof requirement and identification/nonconcealment/support/protection context. Baseline lacks the elevation requirement.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: what bearing condition must a gas-pipe trench provide?
cases.reviewNote: Candidate supplies the firm, substantially continuous bearing on the trench bottom sentence. Baseline lacks a gas-trench bearing rule.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: is underground gas piping beneath a building unconditionally prohibited?
cases.reviewNote: The prohibition and wrought-iron/steel conduit exception with load capacity, corrosion and child-section conditions are present. Not all child details survive in candidate, so evidence is sufficient for this narrow nonabsolute-prohibition question, not complete installation approval.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: how are gas appliances rated below the gas-piping test pressure isolated for testing?
cases.reviewNote: Candidate supplies appliance disconnection and capping when designed operating pressure is less than test pressure, plus leak check after energization. Baseline lacks the disconnection condition.

cases.question: For New York City under the 2022 code edition: may hot ashes be deposited in a combustible container?
cases.reviewNote: Candidate supplies the hot-ash combustible-container prohibition and separation requirements. The exception changes separation distance, not permission to use a combustible container.

cases.question: For New York City under the current Zoning Resolution: must natural grade be disturbed to lower a Manufacturing District yard to curb level?
cases.reviewNote: Both packets retain the Manufacturing District curb-level yard rule and the express natural-grade-disturbance proviso.

cases.question: For New York City under the current Zoning Resolution: what height limit applies to the listed energy infrastructure and accessory mechanical equipment obstruction in an M-district required yard?
cases.reviewNote: Both packets retain the energy-infrastructure/accessory-mechanical-equipment 23-foot-above-curb limit within Manufacturing District required yards, distinct from other obstruction limits.

cases.question: For New York City under the current Zoning Resolution: how are Manufacturing District yard width and depth measured relative to lot lines?
cases.reviewNote: Both packets retain the Manufacturing District requirement to measure yard width/depth perpendicular to lot lines.

cases.question: For New York City under the current Zoning Resolution: what maximum distance applies to required off-site accessory parking spaces in manufacturing districts?
cases.reviewNote: Both packets retain 600 feet measured from the nearest boundary of the served zoning lot plus same/adjoining C8 or Manufacturing District conditions. Baseline target occurs after many alternative-district rules, which increases selection ambiguity but does not remove its decisive text.

cases.question: For New York City under the current Zoning Resolution: can required off-site spaces rely only on a revocable informal arrangement without the specified ownership and recorded deed restrictions?
cases.reviewNote: Both packets retain same ownership including permitted zoning-lot alternatives, recorded deed restrictions binding heirs/assigns for the use lifetime, and applicable district regulations. The ordinary-language question omits Manufacturing District scope; multiple district families are retrieved, so the answer must identify applicability rather than assume it.
